summary: Cite both verses covered by the quotation
rationale: The supplied 77/32 has the opening address “barṯi, d obenax lu abro du qaḏ̣i”; 77/33 has “Hiye ste, kətle mal ġalabe. Gḥoyutu hat w hiye, lə ksənqutu l noše.” The example joins the two consecutive verses. Keep 33 and extend the reference to include 32.

summary: Assign vineyard livelihood at 81/2 to construction 1b.
rationale: mine m-u=karm-ano encodes the means of subsistence, not merely living at a place.

summary: New sense 1b: (mit m-) von etw. leben, seinen Lebensunterhalt aus etw. beziehen;

data.label: 1b
data.gloss: (mit m-) von etw. leben, seinen Lebensunterhalt aus etw. beziehen;

rationale: The vineyard supplies subsistence, not residence. The existing Infectum-wa 81/2 and new Infectum 81/20 support the livelihood construction; separate it without renumbering leben.

data.turoyo: Ḥoyewa eba malko, Abgar Malko əmmiwayle.
data.translation: Darin lebte ein König, den nannte man König Abgar.

rationale: Thin Infectum-wa sense 1 cell; compact named-king context.

data.turoyo: Kətle mal ġalabe w gḥayyat hat w hiye, lo kosənqutu l noše.
data.translation: Er hat viel Geld und gut; du und er, ihr werdet leben, ohne anderer Leute zu bedürfen.

rationale: Thin Infectum sense 1 cell; singular agreement with the first of coordinated participants.

data.turoyo: Ono kal koḥoyeno w an naʕimayḏi mu karmayḏi.
data.translation: Ich und meine Kinder leben von meinem Weinberg.

rationale: First Infectum example for livelihood subsense; 1sg agreement with first conjunct.

summary: New idiom: ḥayyaykum alla 'Gott sei mit euch!' (arabische Grussformel)

data.headword: ḥayyaykum alla 'Gott sei mit euch!' (arabische Grussformel)
data.translation: Er sagte: "ya ḥaiyäikum 'alla ya ʕarab!" Das heißt: "Gott sei mit euch! Eure kraft sei mit euch, ihr Araber!"

rationale: Lookup ḥayya found no greeting; the borrowed/code-switched Arabic formula is explicitly labeled and is not used to establish Stem II. Preserve source ḥayyaykum without normalizing it.

summary: Condolence ḥoye rišo and praise ḥoyən ʕayne are already listed; 2/107 is not re-added. The free wish at 28/8 is already an Infectum example.

77/30 has gḥayyat with the female addressee as first conjunct, whereas 77/33 has plural Gḥoyutu for the same coordinated participants. 81/20 similarly has 1sg koḥoyeno before the coordinated children. These agreement patterns do not establish new meanings.
The Arabic greeting at 29/362 has the Arabic object ending -kum and divine subject alla. It is retained only as a labeled formula; a new Turoyo II stem and base forms are not inferred.
Livelihood m- is separated as 1b; locative b-/eba with living remains 1. No new Detransitive or Preterit box is established by the evidence.
Should the glossary retain fully Arabic greeting formulas as labeled contact material? The formula is isolated from the Turoyo paradigm here.
Is the source spelling ḥayyaykum a phonetic variant or a transcription issue? It is preserved verbatim.
